main_topics.reason: The opening question was whether endo 'burns out' at menopause, and the first several turns covered the outlook and caveats.
The user was nervous about HRT because estrogen may feed endo, and several turns covered combined versus estrogen-only options.
The user asked what to do next so they could go to the primary care follow-up prepared, and the bot gave a concrete list.
The user raised a past surgery with adhesions near the bowel, which affects expectations of improvement, and discussed it briefly.
The user said these are getting rough and are the reason HRT came up, but they were not explored in themselves.
The user asked in one turn whether pain returning on HRT would be obvious or subtle.
The user said in one turn that doctors treat endo as just about periods, and the bot validated this.
Irregular periods and early hot flashes were mentioned once as background.
The user said in passing that they have had enough disappointment with the disease and want an honest picture.

output.summary: A user with long-standing endometriosis who is entering perimenopause asked whether endo improves after menopause. The bot explained the likely improvement and the caveats, including deep disease and adhesions. They then discussed the worry about HRT and estrogen and how to prepare for a primary care follow-up. The user said they felt clearer and better prepared. No safety-critical moments arose.
